judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single truncated sentence stating the core performance obligation; nothing elastic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Agreement Article 2 and its revised Addendum counterpart.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear non-waiver rule tied to specified categories of activity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.2.3 and with Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1's disclaimer of Owner responsibility.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It imposes a study-and-compare duty while disclaiming that the duty is 'for the purpose of discovering errors', a tension that is well known but expressly addressed in the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1(b) makes the Contractor responsible for verifying measurements and bars extra charges, which hardens this obligation beyond what 3.2.1 says.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'In the Contractor's capacity as a contractor and not as a licensed design professional' draws a clear line, though the reporting duty is broad.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 3.12.7.1 requires warranted, trade-expert and sometimes engineer-prepared shop drawings, which edges toward design responsibility.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Dense and partly garbled, but the allocation — Claims under 4.3.6/4.3.7 and Contractor liability for knowing failures — is stated in specific terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 bars claims not embodied in Change Orders, which restricts the Claim route this paragraph presupposes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The warranty exclusions ('improper or insufficient maintenance, improper operation, or normal wear and tear and normal usage') and 'may be considered defective' are open-textured, and the transcription is fragmentary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.2.5 and A201 12.2 correction obligations run alongside it consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Sales, consumer, use and similar taxes' with a timing test tied to bids or negotiations; workable but the 'similar taxes' catch-all is open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.6.2 makes such taxes a reimbursable Cost of the Work and Exhibit D prescribes a Hawaii excise tax methodology with its own exemptions, so who bears which taxes is set in three places.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Customarily secured after execution of the Contract' is a trade-practice test but is conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.6.3 makes permit fees reimbursable, and A201 2.2.2 carves permits out of the Owner's obligations, which together are coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short compliance obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits with 3.7.3 and 3.7.4 without tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear allocation with a notification duty and a Modification route for changes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1 requires compliance with the more stringent of the Contract Documents and applicable codes at the Contractor's own hand, which pulls against this disclaimer.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Appropriate responsibility' is imprecise but the trigger — performing Work knowing it to be contrary to law without notice — is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.7.3 and with 8.1.6's exclusion of costs from Contractor fault.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable objection' is the only soft term in an otherwise mechanical allowance rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 5.2.4 states no allowances at all, so this machinery has nothing to operate on in this contract.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise three-limb accounting rule for what allowances cover and how Change Orders adjust them.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It adjusts 'the Contract Sum' while Article 5 frames payment around Cost of the Work plus Fee with a blank GMP, and no allowances were stated in 5.2.4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'In sufficient time to avoid delay' is a soft timing standard but a familiar one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No allowances are stated in the Agreement, so the obligation is untethered.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Competent superintendent and necessary assistants' and the distinction between 'important communications' and other communications are both unmeasured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum Article 2 requires one designated supervisory employee personally responsible for the project, and 14.4 names a Contractor representative, so three provisions describe site leadership.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable time to review submittals' is soft but ordinary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Conditions 3.10.4 and 3.10.5 govern the construction schedule with a different regime, and Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 adds the Owner to every Architect approval.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'In general accordance with the most recent schedules' is a deliberately loose standard whose enforceability parties dispute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 3.10.4 makes the Construction Schedule part of the Contract Documents, which is a stronger commitment than 'general accordance'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A concrete record-keeping obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Agreement Article 11's records requirement and Supplementary Condition 9.10.1.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition with a specific list of document types.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 3.12.7.1 adds requirements consistent with this definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short definitional provision, partly illegible in transcription.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No competing definition appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition tied to physical examples and standards.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.12.4 and 4.2.7.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: States clearly that submittals are not Contract Documents and confines their purpose.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Conditions 3.10.4 and 3.10.5 make schedules and cost estimates part of the Contract Documents, so the line between contract and non-contract submittals is drawn differently in different places.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable promptness' and 'such sequence as to cause no delay' are ordinary construction standards.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.2.7 and Supplementary Condition 3.12.7.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A deemed representation with specific content ('determined and verified materials, field measurements and field construction criteria').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reinforces Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1(b)'s verification duty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An intricate but carefully conditioned rule about deviations, with two express escape routes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 permits changes only by Change Order, which narrows limb (1)'s written-approval route.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise notice-and-effect rule for resubmittals.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.12.5 and 4.2.7.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long, with several conditional limbs, but each duty and each entitlement to rely is expressly conditioned; the phrase 'unless the Contractor needs to provide such services' is the loosest part.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 3.12.7.1 requires licensed engineer preparation 'if required by the Architect or the Owner or applicable law', which may go further than the criteria-specification bargain here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall not unreasonably encumber the site' is a soft standard but a minor one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No competing site-use provision appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short and definite responsibility allocation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.14.2 and with the Cost of the Work provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall not unreasonably withhold' appears on both sides; the drafting is balanced and specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Article 6 separate-contractor provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Truncated in transcription but the obligation to provide access is simple.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Agreement Article 11's audit and access rights.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exception for designs 'required by the Contract Documents' and the 'reason to believe' qualifier are contestable but conventionally drawn.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.6.5 expressly deals with royalties as a Cost of the Work and cross-refers to the last sentence of this paragraph, so the two must be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To the fullest extent permitted by law' and 'only to the extent caused by the negligent acts or omissions' are carefully bounded, though indemnities of this kind are frequently litigated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is expressed as applying to the extent claims are not covered by Project Management Protective Liability insurance under Paragraph 11.3, yet Agreement Article 16 states no insurance requirements at all.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short anti-limitation rule with a clear referent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.18.1 and with the workers' compensation coverage evidenced in Exhibit E.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition identifying the Architect by reference to the Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Agreement names Fung/Howerson as Architect, so the definition has a referent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear restriction requiring tripartite written consent, with a reasonableness proviso.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 unilaterally adds an Owner consent requirement to every Architect approval, which arguably modifies the Architect's authority without the tripartite consent this paragraph demands.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Badly garbled in transcription, but the substance — successor Architect subject to no reasonable objection — is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 14.5 addresses changes of representatives separately and consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Will be an Owner's representative' with authority 'only to the extent provided in the Contract Documents' is a familiar but somewhat circular formulation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 reserves parallel rights to the Owner while disclaiming Owner responsibility, which complicates the Architect's representative role.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain disclaimer of the Architect's responsibility for the Contractor's acts.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.1.3, 4.2.7 and Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall endeavor to communicate ... through the Architect' is hortatory rather than mandatory, which blurs its effect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 requires direct written notice to the Owner in every case where the Architect must be notified, which cuts across the channel this paragraph sets.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is fragmentary in transcription, but the certification function it describes is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.1.1, 12.2.3 and Supplementary Condition 9.10.1.1 add Owner-side conditions to certification, which layer onto this provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long and heavily garbled, but its limits on the purpose of review ('only for the limited purpose of checking for conformance') are precisely stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 3.12.7.1 requires Architect approval of all shop drawings and adds Contractor warranties, consistent in direction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A very short, partly illegible statement of the Architect's change authority.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 confines changes to Change Orders except under 7.3 and 9.7.1, so the minor-change authority under 7.4 must be reconciled with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Transcription is broken, but the described functions — determining Substantial Completion and issuing the final Certificate — are standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 9.10.1.1 conditions the final Certificate on Owner acceptance of warranties, and Agreement 12.2.3 imposes its own sequence and time limits.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conditional on agreement, with duties 'as set forth in an exhibit'; the exhibit is not identified here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No such exhibit is enumerated in Agreement 15.1.7, which lists only Exhibits A-E on rates, tools, insurance and tax.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable promptness' with a 15-day backstop is a workable standard, though the delay-recognition rule is intricate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 requires Owner concurrence in Architect responses, which could slow the very interpretations this paragraph times.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Consistent with the intent of and reasonably inferable from the Contract Documents' and good-faith immunity are broad standards for a decision-maker's authority.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 subjects Architect action to Owner approval, which sits uneasily with the requirement that the Architect 'not show partiality to either' party.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Matters relating to aesthetic effect' is undefined and finality is conditioned on consistency with 'the intent expressed in the Contract Documents', which is circular.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 expressly reserves aesthetic control to the Owner, so finality of the Architect's aesthetic decisions is contradicted elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition sweeps in 'other disputes and matters in question ... arising out of or relating to the Contract' after a specific list, an open-ended extension of a defined term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 forecloses whole categories of claim regardless of this definition, and Agreement 12.2.4 allows direct arbitration of accounting disputes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise 21-day limit with a 'whichever is later' alternative trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 4.3.7.3 adds documentation requirements consistent with this timing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear obligation to continue performance and payment pending resolution.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.2.4 similarly requires payment of the certified amount pending arbitration, which is consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Differ materially', 'unusual nature' and 'equitably adjusted' are the classic elastic terms of a differing-site-conditions clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 confines increases to Change Orders and 1.2.1.1(b) bars extra charges for dimensional differences, which narrow this route to relief.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list of grounds is expressly 'including but not limited to' and closes with '(7) other reasonable grounds' — a general catch-all after six specifics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 bars claims founded on course of conduct or unjust enrichment, so the reach of this open-ended claim right is contested by another operative provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A specific content requirement for time claims.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Conditions 4.3.7.3 and 4.3.7.4 supplement and restrict it consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Abnormal for the period of time' and 'could not have been reasonably anticipated' are judgment standards requiring extrinsic data.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 4.3.7.4's bar on separate increases for concurrent causes bears on weather claims but does not contradict this.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A reasonable time not exceeding 21 days' and 'sufficient detail' are bounded standards.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.3.2 and with the insurance provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Materially changed' and 'substantial inequity' are open standards, and the remedy is an unspecified 'equitable adjustment'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 5.2.3 states no unit prices, so this paragraph has no subject matter in this contract unless prices are 'subsequently agreed upon'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mutual waiver with two illustrative lists and a saving for 'liquidated direct damages, when applicable' — the interaction of the enumerated categories with the general waiver is a familiar battleground.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Agreement inserted no liquidated damages provision in 4.3 and the Addendum's 4.4 bonus is one-directional, so the saving clause has nothing to save.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Five enumerated options with a ten-day deadline; the 'sole discretion' escape in option (5) is broad but expressly conferred.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.2.4 lets the Contractor demand arbitration 'without a further decision of the Architect', bypassing this review for final-accounting disputes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permissive and short.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.4.2 and with Agreement 12.2.3's use of the Owner's accountants.
